BLOCKER: New network + secret-handling logic (`_api_key()`, `_llm_call()`, response-shape parsing) ships with zero test coverage — no unit tests for key resolution, request construction, empty/`reasoning_content` fallback, or HTTP failure paths. The item's own `verification` field records this as a Gate 2.5 blocker, yet the diff contains no tests.

Backlog data integrity: `BI-PF-1428` was removed from `BI-PF-1252.execution_order` but only re-appended to `children` — it is now a child of the epic with no execution slot, so epic orchestration will never schedule it.
MAJOR: Config contract is silently ignored: `architect-review.json` declares `api_key_env: OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY` and `api_key_file: .opencode/opencode.key`, but `_api_key()` hardcodes different env names (`OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY`, `PF_ARCHITECT_REVIEW_KEY`) and different file paths (`ROOT/.opencode/opencode.key`, `ROOT/opencode.key`). An operator honoring the documented config gets an unexplained "no API key" failure or the wrong key. Either honor the config keys or delete them.

Stale/misleading config: `launch_command` and `agent` are now dead keys, and the config `description` still says the reviewer "is launched as a separate fresh-context sub-agent" — which is no longer true. Config drift will mislead future maintainers.

The analysis promised "keep `core/llm_error_handler.py` for retries and `core/call_ledger.py` for call accounting" and "CLI path remains as a fallback behind a feature flag". The implementation does neither: raw `urllib` with a single attempt, no retry/backoff on 429/5xx, no call-ledger accounting, no usage recording, and the CLI fallback (`launch_command`/`PF_ARCHITECT_REVIEW_CMD`) was deleted outright. The shipped design diverges from the approved architecture record.

"Provider- and model-AGNOSTIC" claim is broken by vendor coupling in code: the `x-opencode-session` header (random UUID per call, so no real session affinity) and the pinned `User-Agent: opencode/1.18.35` are OpenCode-specific and hardcoded in the fallback path, not config.

Process integrity: `context_review` recorded `ok: false`, `implementable: false`, and `decision_request.needed: true` (missing_info/unimplementable), yet the item was auto-approved (`APPROVE by system`), marked `readiness.ready: true`, and the `decision_request` was later flipped to `needed: false` with no answering of the open questions. `reasoning_content` is accepted as a valid review output fallback and ingested as findings — this can inject raw chain-of-thought into `engineering/reviews/*.json` and downstream `--apply` summary writes.

Secret hygiene: key material is read from a repo-relative `.opencode/opencode.key` / `opencode.key` with errors swallowed (`except Exception: pass`), encouraging committing secrets to the repo tree and masking permission/corruption failures. Prefer env/secret-manager resolution with explicit, logged failures and a `.gitignore` guarantee.

`max_tokens` hardcoded to 4000 with no truncation detection; a long review will be silently cut off and ingested as complete (BI-PF-1196 truncation risk was explicitly a dependency).

SUMMARY: The direction is right — direct OpenAI-compatible calls eliminate a fragile nested-CLI spawn — but the change ships as a hardcoded, vendor-coupled path that ignores its own config contract, drops the promised retries/ledger/fallback, and has zero test coverage on new secret-handling code. Combined with an epic data defect that strands BI-PF-1428 and an auto-approval that overrode an explicit "not implementable" finding, this needs fixes on integrity (config honored, execution_order restored) and robustness (tests, retries, logging) before merge.
